observed.source: Codex session rollout (CLI-recorded thread settings; not model-authored)

result.decision_rationale:
The required unit gate passed, and the fixtures demonstrate a complete correction cycle. Changes are required because the controller can apply an amendment while restoration is outstanding, replay a superseded request, and block a valid multiline continuation before Claude receives it.

## Continuation for Claude

Correct amendment admission and publication retirement together. Use the recorded restoration and process outcomes, reconcile uncertain comment deliveries against the enrolled PR, and retire visible obsolete work before the next developer invocation. Check that a cumulative amendment can be published before selecting it. Preserve distinct owner messages and the instruction binding of each returned report.

Keep the authenticated reviewer rationale unchanged and make its public rendering survive a Windows line-ending round trip. Align the operator instructions with the status evidence, activation states and budget controls the controller actually provides. Exercise the cases below through the existing Git and controller fixtures, including a cited reviewer assessment and an enforced project gate. Run `unit` through `verify` on the pushed correction. The existing schema, model policy, permissions, budgets and single-writer design support these corrections.

executed_verification: I confirmed the detached HEAD, the history-preserving merge of main, and a clean `git diff --check` for M..H. Both mission files match the supplied SHA-256.

The developer CLI transcript records the guarded push of 7add367b6274fd58af3b2bb49272a203f4624061 and the pinned controller's `verify --gate unit` invocation. The candidate-bound receipt records exit 0, 600.7 seconds and an unchanged worktree. I verified the log digest against the receipt. The log records 244 tests run with one skipped.

The transcript records nine focused continuation and amendment tests passing before commit. The candidate gate log also records all nine passing, including publication, archive, fresh-session continuation and a simulated owner handoff.
inspected: The complete mission and owner addendum, AGENTS.md, the operating guide, protocol section 10, the feature diff, developer report, transcript, gate artifacts and empty prior-findings ledger.
Controller admission, report acceptance, prompt construction, publication reconciliation, supersession, readiness, status and activation paths, together with their behavior fixtures.
limitations: I used the controller-recorded test results in the read-only snapshot. The failure paths identified below come from source inspection.

The candidate fixtures simulate Claude, Codex and GitHub. The supplemental live-model gates were not run. Notification in the launching conversation and post-acceptance activation remain supervisor and owner actions.
required_gaps: The withdrawal fixture needs a reviewer assessment that identifies the amendment and explains the withdrawn requirement.
The amendment fixtures need an actual required project gate and evidence that report correction retains the amended task while that gate is outstanding.
The corrections need focused observations for the restoration, publication, continuation and instruction-history cases below, followed by a passing gate on the corrected commit.
source_inspection_only: Traced how an incomplete restoration, a lost POST response, a partially published request and an accepted ready result interact with amendment application.
Traced CRLF rationale publication, cumulative-document validation, report history and the operator commands against their production consumers.

acceptance_ids: B. Apply at the next safe boundary, without re-enrollment
findings.actual: `accept_report()` persists the pending restoration and pauses. Amendment admission checks lock files but ignores that report, so it can select the amendment and dispatch Claude. Its lock check also precedes GitHub reads that `retire_verdict()` or `retire_receipts()` can perform during application.
findings.blocking_rationale: The task can change and another invocation can begin before the controller has established the required restoration boundary.
findings.expected: Keep the update pending while the controller has affirmative evidence of unfinished restoration. Check shared runtime locks after any remote reconciliation needed for the transition.
findings.requested_correction: Include the recorded restoration outcome in amendment admission and place the final runtime-lock check after potentially slow retirement observations, immediately before committing the application.
findings.requested_evidence: Have a developer return `runtime_restoration: pending` with no lock file and show refusal with unchanged selection and invocation count. Also exercise a shared lock appearing during the last publication lookup.
findings.title: Amendment admission can pass with restoration still pending
findings.trigger: A developer returns a report declaring restoration pending, and no configured runtime lock is present when the supervisor applies the saved update.

acceptance_ids: B. Apply at the next safe boundary, without re-enrollment
findings.actual: `amendment_refusal()` treats every `posting_since` without a local comment ID as uncertain. It never calls the existing authenticated reconciliation path. Its prescribed ordinary resume can finish the obsolete request and launch its reviewer.
findings.blocking_rationale: An idle, verifiable review boundary can require another model invocation under the superseded task.
findings.expected: Accept a uniquely matched comment from the expected actor on the enrolled PR. Refuse unchanged while the outcome remains ambiguous.
findings.requested_correction: After verifying target identity, reconcile outstanding POST markers and bodies read-only during admission. Persist confirmed references with the amendment transaction and retain refusal for absent, conflicting or unverifiable matches.
findings.requested_evidence: Lose a simulated POST response, let the stored comment become visible before amendment admission, and show one comment, zero obsolete reviewer calls and successful application. Keep an ambiguous-delivery refusal case.
findings.title: A lost POST response blocks an amendment even after delivery is verifiable
findings.trigger: The controller pauses during publication, then the exact stored comment becomes visible on the PR before the supervisor applies the update.

acceptance_ids: B. Apply at the next safe boundary, without re-enrollment
findings.actual: A request is withdrawn only when none of its parts has a comment ID. A partly delivered request stays `pending`, so `develop_step()` calls `settle_publications()` and sends its remaining parts after supersession. At the finalize boundary, an accepted ready verdict with no handoff receipt is superseded only in private state.
findings.blocking_rationale: The PR can receive an obsolete request after the update or continue to show a ready verdict without a visible supersession. Retrying the obsolete request can also hold up current development.
findings.expected: Retain delivered history, withdraw unsent parts, and identify publicly visible work whose request or readiness has been superseded.
findings.requested_correction: Retire the stopped round's request regardless of its delivered-part count. Use the existing correction and archive mechanisms for visible parts and for a published ready verdict superseded before a handoff receipt exists.
findings.requested_evidence: Apply an amendment after part one is posted and part two is definitively rejected. Verify the public correction, archived delivered parts and absence of a later send for part two. Also stop after an accepted ready verdict and verify its public supersession.
findings.title: Superseding a round leaves some of its public work current
findings.trigger: An amendment arrives after partial delivery of a multipart request, or after the ready review is published but before the handoff receipt.

findings.actual: `review_body()` embeds the rationale directly. `queue()` hashes the CRLF text, while `outbox_body()` reads the saved file with universal newline translation and hashes LF text. The pre-send integrity check reports a modified body and stops the round.
findings.blocking_rationale: A schema-valid reviewer continuation can stop before publication, acceptance and delivery to Claude.
findings.expected: The public review survives its write/read integrity check, and the developer prompt uses the original rationale from the authenticated private envelope.
findings.requested_correction: Use consistent line endings when hashing and reading the public rendering. Preserve the private rationale. Clarify the README's byte-exact claim since the committed envelope is reserialized with publication metadata and sanitized.
findings.requested_evidence: Return a distinctive CRLF rationale from simulated Codex and take it through publication, the following developer prompt, archive and verified handoff. Check the public rendering and private rationale separately.
findings.title: CRLF in the reviewer's continuation prevents publication
findings.trigger: Codex returns a multiline `decision_rationale` containing CRLF separators.

acceptance_ids: B. Both roles receive the same effective instructions
findings.actual: Admission checks encoding, size and digest. The existing strict sanitizer first sees the cumulative text when the review request is queued, after the amendment has superseded prior work and a developer invocation can already have run. Every later cumulative revision retains the offending text.
findings.blocking_rationale: A rejected public rendering can prevent subsequent reviews in the same enrollment even after the supervisor supplies a publishable correction.
findings.expected: Detect input that the existing publication policy will refuse while the instruction is still pending with the supervisor.
findings.requested_correction: Preflight the prospective amendment rendering with the existing strict sanitizer before selection or retirement. Preserve the exact private bytes for accepted input.
findings.requested_evidence: Use harmless text containing a lone PEM opening delimiter. Show an unchanged local refusal, followed by successful application and publication of a PR-safe update in the same enrollment.
findings.title: An unpublishable message can become permanent amendment history
findings.trigger: A valid UTF-8 update contains text the existing sanitizer refuses, such as a quoted, unmatched private-key opening delimiter.

findings.actual: Admission compares only the message digest with the latest amendment and refuses identical bytes, including a separately saved message received after the previous instruction was delivered and implemented.
findings.blocking_rationale: The supervisor cannot preserve and apply each distinct owner decision verbatim in order.
findings.expected: A separately received owner instruction can create another labeled entry even when the owner uses the same words.
findings.requested_correction: Distinguish replay of the same saved submission from a newly received message using the existing capture metadata. Preserve both entries for distinct submissions.
findings.requested_evidence: Apply a message, complete the requested work, then apply a new timestamped saved message with identical bytes. Verify both labeled messages in order in the effective task.
findings.title: Distinct owner decisions with identical wording are refused
findings.trigger: After the first update is implemented, the owner again says “Add one more acceptance example.” The supervisor saves that new decision in a separate pending file.

acceptance_ids: B. Apply at the next safe boundary, without re-enrollment
findings.actual: Admission accepts `done` only with status `AWAITING_OWNER_REVIEW`, although ordinary resume recognizes a handoff by phase after an operational pause. It also checks PID liveness for every reviewer attempt before checking its recorded end. An unrelated process reusing a finished reviewer's PID causes refusal.
findings.blocking_rationale: Both conditions reject idle enrollments within the requested support boundary and can steer the supervisor into resuming obsolete work.
findings.expected: Use the recorded handoff and attempt completion to establish eligibility, together with the current PR identity and live-work checks.
findings.requested_correction: Recognize a preserved handoff in a stopped `done` phase after rechecking the open draft PR. Apply reviewer liveness checks to unfinished attempts.
findings.requested_evidence: Exercise a completed handoff whose ordinary resume paused during a temporary PR-read failure, and a stopped review whose ended attempt has a reused PID. Verify application without an obsolete launch and preserve refusal for an unfinished attempt.
findings.title: Admission can mistake a completed handoff or reviewer attempt for an ineligible state
findings.trigger: The enrollment retains its handoff after an operational pause in `done`, or a stopped review contains an ended attempt whose PID has since been reused.

acceptance_ids: B. Both roles receive the same effective instructions
findings.actual: `reports[]` stores only the timestamp and report. Only the latest checkpoint-ready report gets `last_report_amendments`. A subsequent paused or blocked report replaces `last_report` while leaving that companion binding at the earlier revision. A report superseded before a review round has no round record to supply its binding.
findings.blocking_rationale: The controller loses the required historical association between a returned report and the task it answered, even though commit freshness prevents the stopped report from passing readiness.
findings.expected: A stored report retains the revision and digest from its returning invocation through later stops and selections.
findings.requested_correction: Record the existing instruction bindings alongside each persisted report and keep the binding accompanying `last_report` consistent with the report it names. Retain `last_report_for` as the freshness guard.
findings.requested_evidence: Return reports on the same commit under two revisions, including a pause before a review request. Reload state and verify each report's historical binding and the current report's eligibility.
findings.title: Historical developer reports lose their instruction binding
findings.trigger: A later amendment supersedes a developer report before its review request, or the next amended invocation returns a paused or blocked report.

acceptance_ids: B. Both roles receive the same effective instructions
findings.actual: The playbook identifies `latest_review_round.matches_selected` together with `selected.first_returned_invocation` as evidence of inclusion. The former is populated when the round is allocated, and the latter records only a developer return. Both can be set while `latest_attempt` is null and no reviewer prompt exists.
findings.blocking_rationale: Following the operator instructions can produce a false report that the reviewer received the updated task.
findings.expected: Supervisors can distinguish an allocated round, a prepared input, a process start and a returned result for the relevant role.
findings.requested_correction: Explain the amendment status fields using the existing per-role launch and attempt evidence. State what can be reported when request publication stops before a reviewer attempt opens.
findings.requested_evidence: Show the status for an amended round stopped before reviewer dispatch and for a completed amended review. The playbook should yield an accurate delivery statement in each case.
findings.title: The operator playbook overstates evidence of reviewer delivery
findings.trigger: The amended developer returns, the controller allocates a matching review round, and publication fails before reviewer input preparation.

acceptance_ids: B. Apply at the next safe boundary, without re-enrollment
findings.actual: Activating a new version at an owner handoff changes the enrollment to `ACTIVE` in `review`. The documented immediate `resume --amend-mission` then refuses. The amendment section also presents `--max-rounds` as recovery for an exhausted budget, although it cannot extend the developer-invocation cap.
findings.blocking_rationale: The requested post-acceptance and recovery instructions give commands that cannot advance these supported cases.
findings.expected: The documented next command reaches an eligible amendment boundary and identifies the specific limit that requires an owner decision.
findings.requested_correction: Document the post-activation status branch. For an activated handoff with the cooperative stop still present, show how to reach `PAUSED` before applying the pending file without dispatching the old review. Scope the `--max-rounds` remedy to the review-round cap.
findings.requested_evidence: Trace the documented stop, activation and amendment commands on an existing-handoff fixture. Cross-check the two budget remedies against their separate controller limits.
findings.title: The handoff activation and budget instructions need state-specific commands
findings.trigger: A supervisor activates the reviewed package on an existing handoff with an owner update pending, or encounters an exhausted developer-invocation budget after application.

acceptance_ids: B. Preserve findings while reassessing applicability
findings.actual: The developer disposition cites `OWNER AMENDMENT 1`, but the simulated reviewer's accepted assessment has only `rationale: "simulated"`. The test checks the assessment enum. The reviewer prompt tells Codex to verify the developer's citation without asking it to identify the amendment and changed requirement in its own rationale.
findings.blocking_rationale: The required retained reviewer assessment citing the amendment is missing from the demonstrated withdrawal cycle.
findings.expected: The review assessment identifies the withdrawing amendment and explains its applicability, while the unrelated defect remains blocking.
findings.requested_correction: Make the citation explicit in the reviewer prompt and exercise it through the existing assessment rationale, publication and ledger fields.
findings.requested_evidence: Inspect the accepted review and retained assessment for the amendment label and reason the specific requirement was withdrawn. Keep the existing assertion that the unrelated defect stays open.
findings.title: The withdrawal fixture lacks the reviewer's amendment citation
findings.trigger: The reviewer accepts the developer's rebuttal of a historically valid finding under the amended task.

findings.actual: The amendment fixture compares the saved project configuration, but its `required_gates` list is empty and its plan adds none. The passing suite therefore does not exercise a required project gate on an amended report.
findings.blocking_rationale: Preserving an enforced project gate across application is an explicit behavior-test requirement. The candidate's own successful unit gate establishes a different observation.
findings.expected: An amended candidate still needs a passing receipt for its configured required gate before review.
findings.requested_correction: Exercise application in a fixture with a nonempty required project gate. Use the missing receipt on a new commit to exercise the amended report-correction invocation as well.
findings.requested_evidence: Show the report being rejected before reviewer dispatch, the correction prompt carrying the selected amendment, and the candidate proceeding after the real fixture gate records its passing receipt.
findings.title: Gate preservation after an amendment is tested with an empty gate set
findings.trigger: An owner amendment is applied and the developer submits a report for a new candidate before obtaining its required receipt.

summary.delivered_behavior: The ordinary fixture cycle forwards an authenticated reviewer rationale to continued and fresh developer sessions, publishes and archives the review, and reaches a verified handoff. The amendment path captures cumulative messages, delivers them to both roles, preserves approach guidance and requires a fresh report on unchanged source.
remaining_owner_review: After a corrected candidate reaches a verified handoff, the owner decides whether to accept [draft PR #6](https://github.com/howardreith/development-process/pull/6) and authorize installation or activation for any existing enrollment.
summary.scope_reviewed: Complete final-checkpoint mission at 7add367b6274fd58af3b2bb49272a203f4624061, including reviewer continuation, same-enrollment owner updates, operator procedures and candidate-bound validation.
